newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris tobacco, US food revs boost Q2.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris tobacco, US food revs boost Q2.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc, reporting higher second quarter results, cited strength in its domestic and international tobacco businesses and its North American food operations.
The company said second quarter earnings rose to $1.8 billion, or $0.76 per share, up from $1.6 billion, or $0.66 per share, a year earlier.
It said worldwide tobacco income grew 13 percent to $2.3 billion, on revenues of $10.2 billion, up 10.4 percent.
Philip Morris sold 238 billion cigarettes in the second quarter, up 6.8 percent from a year earlier.

Domestic tobacco revenues climbed to $3.5 billion from $3.1 billion a year ago. The company attributed the gains to higher volume and gross margins, and a continued shift in sales to more profitable premium brands.
It said its Marlboro brand of cigarettes now has a 34.6 percent share of industry sales, up 3.2 percentage points over the same period in 1996.

International tobacco revenues rose 10.5 percent to $6.7 billion, on higher volume and margins. The gains were partially offset by the stronger dollar, mainly against key European currencies and the Japanese yen.

Revenues from North American food operations increased to $4.3 billion in the second quarter from $4.2 billion last year, led by strong results within the Kraft Foods North America unit, Philip Morris said.
Volume for Maxwell House and other coffee brands declined during the quarter due to very heavy first-quarter buying in advance of commodity-driven price increases, and lower coffee consumption.
International food revenues fell 3.6 percent to $2.6 billion, due primarily to the impact of currency.
Philip Morris said its second quarter beer revenues were up slightly to $1.2 billion.

"Our domestic tobacco business is performing well, our international tobacco business is forging ahead, and our North American food operations are turning in stellar results," said Geoffrey Bible, Philip Morris chairman and chief executive, in a written statement.
